# Regenerate CDDL Codegen

Use whenever `dev/cddl/{parser,generator,utils}.ex` or `priv/cddl/*.cddl`
changes. The codegen overwrites at paths it computes; when those paths shift
(e.g. acronym handling, snake_case rules), stale files linger unless you
nuke + regen.

## Steps

```bash
# 1. Wipe every generated file (run from packages/bibbidi/)
grep -rl "Generated by mix bibbidi.gen" lib/ | xargs rm

# 2. Regenerate from CDDL + dev/
mix bibbidi.gen --yes

# 3. Eyeball the diff
git status

# 4. Verify nothing broke
mix test
```

## Notes

- The marker `# Generated by mix bibbidi.gen — do not edit manually` is on
  every generated file. The grep is safe — hand-written files
  (e.g. `Bibbidi.Events.Unknown`) lack the marker and survive.
- Clean working tree after regen = your change was effectively a no-op.
  Focused diff = intentional behaviour change. Unexpected diff = bug.
- If `mix bibbidi.gen` fails with a CompileError on a previously-generated
  file, an earlier run wrote broken Elixir. Recover with
  `git checkout -- lib/` and rerun — your codegen changes in `dev/` are
  untouched.
- `mix run -e 'IO.inspect(Bibbidi.CDDL.Utils.to_snake("Foo"))'` etc. is the
  quickest way to verify a single naming rule without a full regen.
